steps.name: Count matrix and metadata QC
steps.question: Do the raw counts.csv (12000 genes x 6 samples) and metadata.csv (6 samples, condition: 3 treated / 3 control) agree on sample identity, and do library size, gene-detection rate, sample correlation, and PCA structure look consistent with the stated unpaired single-batch 3-vs-3 design, or do they show signs of outlier/mislabeled samples?
acceptance_criteria: Sample names in counts.csv columns are matched 1:1 to metadata.csv rows with no unmatched or duplicated identifiers
Per-sample library size (column sum), gene detection rate (count>0 fraction), and a log-CPM distribution are reported for all 6 samples
A sample-sample correlation matrix and a PCA (on variance-stabilized counts) are produced and visually checked against the condition labels
Any sample flagged as an outlier (e.g. >3x median library size, or clustering opposite its labeled condition) is explicitly named and the deviation quantified, without being excluded outright

steps.name: Strand-setting count-integrity diagnostic
steps.question: Given that the library's strandedness was never recorded and no BAM/FASTQ is available to run a direct strand-inference tool (e.g. RSeQC infer_experiment), does the human GENCODE GRCh38 gene annotation, applied to this liver count matrix, show any indirect signature of a strand-setting problem at counting time — specifically among genes with antisense-overlapping neighbors, and among canonical highly-expressed liver genes (ALB, APOA1, APOB, TTR, SERPINA1, HP, TF)?
acceptance_criteria: Gene coordinates and strand are parsed from the GENCODE GRCh38 annotation and used to flag, for every gene symbol present in counts.csv, whether it has an antisense-overlapping neighboring gene (overlap_ambiguous TRUE/FALSE)
Median log-CPM is compared between overlap-flagged and non-overlap genes across the 6 samples, reported as a table/plot
Counts for the named canonical high-expression liver genes are reported per sample and assessed for plausibility (i.e., not near-zero)

A written conclusion states whether the evidence is consistent with a plausible strand setting or shows signs of gross mis-assignment, and explicitly notes that this is an indirect check, not a substitute for BAM-level strand inference which this dataset cannot support
The overlap_ambiguous gene-level flag table is saved for use by the annotation step

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression, treated vs control
steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes are differentially expressed between the 3 treated and 3 control liver samples (unpaired, single batch), using DESeq2 with design ~ condition?
acceptance_criteria: A DESeqDataSet is built from the raw integer counts and the condition column of metadata.csv, with treated vs control as the contrast
Genes with negligible counts (row sum < 10 across all 6 samples) are filtered before testing
DESeq2's Wald test is run and log2 fold changes are shrunk with apeglm
A full results table (gene, baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, pvalue, padj) is exported sorted by padj
Dispersion-estimate plot, PCA on VST-transformed counts, sample-distance heatmap, MA plot, and a volcano plot (padj<0.05, |log2FC|>1 highlighted) are produced
The report explicitly states that with n=3 per group, statistical power is limited and the gene list is a working hypothesis set

steps.name: Annotate DE results with strand-risk flag and test for confound
steps.question: Among genes reaching padj<0.05 in the treated-vs-control DESeq2 result, are strand-risk (antisense-overlap-ambiguous) genes over-represented relative to the tested background — i.e., is the unresolved strandedness a plausible driver of the apparent differential expression signal?
acceptance_criteria: The DESeq2 results table from T1S3 is merged with the overlap_ambiguous flag from T1S2 by gene symbol
A Fisher's exact test compares the proportion of overlap_ambiguous genes among padj<0.05 hits versus the full tested background
The final annotated table (all DE statistics plus the ambiguity flag) is exported
The enrichment test result and its interpretation (confound risk high/low) are stated explicitly as a caveat on the DE result set

steps.name: Pathway enrichment on DE genes, full vs strand-risk-filtered
steps.question: Which WikiPathways and MSigDB Hallmark pathways are enriched among genes differentially expressed between treated and control liver samples, and do the enriched pathways change when strand-risk (antisense-overlap-ambiguous) genes are removed from the significant gene list?
acceptance_criteria: Over-representation analysis is run on the padj<0.05 DE gene set (from T1S4) against human WikiPathways gene sets and human MSigDB Hallmark gene sets
The same enrichment is repeated after excluding overlap_ambiguous genes from the significant set
Top enriched pathways (adjusted p-value, gene overlap) are reported for both runs and any pathways that appear only in the unfiltered run are flagged as strand-risk-sensitive findings
If either reference gene-set file is unavailable at run time, the step reports the gap and proceeds with whichever reference is present

plan.title: Liver drug treatment DE with strand/count-integrity QC
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a bulk RNA-seq gene-level count matrix (12000 genes x 6 samples) from STAR/featureCounts, human liver, 3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch, with metadata.csv (6x2) giving condition. The library's strandedness was never recorded, and no BAM/FASTQ files are available to rerun featureCounts with an explicit strand setting or to run RSeQC infer_experiment directly on aligned reads — so strandedness cannot be measured directly, only its downstream footprint can be inspected in the count matrix itself. The plan therefore front-loads two QC passes before any DE call: (1) a general count-matrix QC (library size, detection rate, sample correlation/PCA) to catch swaps, outliers, or corrupted values, and (2) a targeted count-integrity check that uses the GENCODE GRCh38 gene annotation to flag genes with antisense-overlapping neighbors — the class of loci most sensitive to a wrong strand setting at counting time — and checks whether canonical highly-expressed liver genes look plausible. DESeq2 is then run on the full matrix (design ~ condition) with apeglm shrinkage, and its result table is annotated with the overlap-ambiguity flag so a Fisher's-exact enrichment test can check whether 'significant' genes are disproportionately drawn from strand-risk loci — direct evidence for or against a counting artifact rather than real treatment effect. Pathway enrichment (WikiPathways human, MSigDB Hallmark human) is run on both the full and the strand-risk-filtered DE gene sets so pathway conclusions are not silently driven by miscounted loci. Every step states explicitly what it can and cannot establish given the missing strandedness metadata and n=3 per group.
